about: Rigby's speed arsenal as data (the owner 2026-10-14: 'take a step back and do a review of the arsenal at our disposal and our data ... all the different ways we can store layers, how we can store expert caches, the way to speed things up'). Same schema and rule as mothership-build\workspace\flashnext\arsenal.json: a lever counts as TRIED only when its FULL form ran; partial forms are partial; update a lever's status in the SAME pass its result lands. Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q3_K_XL (16 GB, qwen35moe, 40 layers: 10 full attention + 30 DeltaNet). Box: i7-3770 (AVX+F16C, no AVX2), 4x DDR3-1600 (24 GB), GTX 1060 6 GB on a riser at PCIe 3.0 x1, GT 730 2 GB in a Gen 2 chipset slot, 10 Fellowship tablets on USB 2. Status: open | testing | partial | done | closed | needs-owner | reassign | n/a. 'reassign' = the device's old job is now done faster by another part of the box; the DEVICE is not retired (the owner 2026-10-14: 'idk that anything is superseded due to our philosophy for this being the Frankenstein machine. It's been given more hardware to work with, rather than replacing the hardware ... Ideally we can get everything pinned to maximum') - it needs a new job that stacks with the rest.

Mechanism: with ~52 % of a written token in CPU-held experts, a k-token check sends each token to its own experts, so CPU expert work grows ~k-fold and only the GPU half is batched (n-gram only - MTP measured separately and WINS: r67/r68). r52b (49-token checks) cancelled as known-bad. couplings.why: CUDA's compute buffers differ from Vulkan's - the fitter will place differently; record the placement per order
CUDA graphs lower per-op cost but misses still ride the x1 link
a bigger micro-batch grows the compute buffer the fitter must fit (measured cost to write at 2048: -1 %)
r40 reused 397 cached tokens vs r39's 1,929 at ub 512 - unexplained
the threshold decides which batches stream; ub decides how big a streamed batch is
the cook must know which layers stay CPU-side - take them from the recorded placement
community: checking drafted tokens pulls more experts over the link
each extra slot's context and state come out of the card's memory
the cache's misses are uploads; at x1 it is predicted to lose
